jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer – IoT Platform, Load and Energy Management
jobs.description:
🚀 About the role

We're looking for a senior software engineer who writes solid, reliable code and wants that code to control real hardware. At FLEXECHARGE, our HARMON-E platform manages load and energy for EV charging operators across Europe. Part of it runs at the edge, on an industrial PC next to chargers, batteries and solar inverters, and connected to the interfaces DSOs use to curtail load.

You'll build and maintain the TypeScript microservices that talk to those devices and turn their data into decisions. This is not a web-app role. It's software engineering for systems where the other side is physical, stateful and often unreliable.

⚡ What is special about this role

It sits where two worlds meet:

• 
Web and cloud toolchain: TypeScript, Docker, MQTT, Azure, Kubernetes.

• 
Operational technology and system integration: talking to real chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus and OCPP, running at the edge on an industrial PC.

Your code won't only talk to clean APIs in a data centre. It runs on site, next to real peripheral devices, and has to keep doing its job when those devices and the networks between them don't behave as expected.

We recognize that TypeScript is not typically used for edge computing or hardware interfacing. This is why we're looking for a strong software engineer who is interested in learning new techniques and applications, as well as applying their technical skills in novel ways.

🛠️ What you'll do

• 
Write and maintain a combination of TypeScript microservices and the business logic behind them: control algorithms, scheduling and decision-making, not just plumbing.

• 
Build and extend device drivers for chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus TCP, using our existing driver services as a starting point.

• 
Work with OCPP, which our platform already supports, as you ramp up.

• 
Run services in containers at the edge and connect them through MQTT and pub/sub messaging to our cloud backend.

• 
Profile and optimise software on edge hardware, where hardware resources are constrained.

• 
Help shape the long-term move of performance-critical services to compiled languages.

• 
Mentor and pair with colleagues on integrations and software craft.

🤔 Why compiled languages, if we write TypeScript?

It may sound odd, so here's the reasoning. Today the majority of our edge stack is TypeScript, and you'll develop in it from day one. Over time we want to move selected services, such as device interfaces and performance-critical paths, to a compiled language while keeping them part of the same stack.

To do that well, you need to understand both sides: the TypeScript services as they are now, and the concepts of memory, types and performance that compiled languages force you to think about. In our experience, it's much easier to go from a compiled language to a scripting environment than the other way around. So if you're a Go, C, C++, Rust or similar developer who is happy to work in TypeScript (or happy to learn), you're exactly who we're looking for.

✅ Must-have

• 
3–5+ years of professional software development, with strong software and engineering fundamentals.

• 
Professional experience in a compiled language (for example Go, C, C++, Rust, C# or Java).

• 
Proficiency in a scripting language, ideally TypeScript, otherwise JavaScript or Python, or a clear willingness to become productive in TypeScript quickly.

• 
Experience writing business logic with stateful calculations and operations, which can self-heal and recover gracefully.

• 
Comfort with asynchronous and event-driven systems that talk to unreliable external components or peripheral devices.

💡 Strongly preferred (but we'll teach it)

• 
Hands-on device or protocol integration: Modbus, serial interfaces, Ethernet/TCP-IP or comparable.

• 
Containerised applications. Docker, Docker Compose or Kubernetes are ideal, but any container technology counts.

• 
Pub/sub and distributed systems, ideally MQTT or another IoT messaging protocol, and an understanding of their reliability concerns.

• 
Working within constrained systems, including profiling software to find where CPU or memory limits bite.

🎁 Bonus, not a requirement

• 
OCPP experience.

• 
Energy, EV charging or power-systems domain knowledge.

• 
Edge deployment experience.

If you don't have these, apply anyway. Strong fundamentals and the right mindset matter more. 💪

🚫 This role is probably not for you if

• 
Your experience is mainly frontend or request/response web apps, with no compiled-language background.

• 
You prefer to stay in one language and aren't interested in working in TypeScript.

• 
You want a pure firmware or PLC role without writing higher-level services.

• 
You don't enjoy debugging the messy cases where hardware doesn't behave as documented.

🌆 What is it like to work at FLEXECHARGE?

• 
Our office is in Frederiksberg: bright, comfortable, and a genuinely nice place to spend your workday.

• 
You're covered with pension contributions.

• 
Lunch is served on-site, and it's delicious, healthy and nutritious.

• 
We enjoy each other's company outside work too, with Friday bars, company events and team-building activities within each team.

• 
You'll have opportunities for individual development.

🤝 Our interview process

Here's roughly what happens once we've had a look at your application:

• 
A first conversation (about 30 minutes) with our recruiter. You'll get a feel for the role, ask whatever's on your mind, and we'll both get a sense of whether this is worth pursuing further.

• 
Time with the team: a conversation with Kasper, our Head of Architecture & Systems, and Robert, our CTO.

• 
A technical stage: one or more interviews with the team, which may include a case exercise and follow-up discussions. These can take place remotely or at our office.

• 
A conversation with Max, our CEO, alongside someone else from the team.

Hiring carefully matters to us. We want to get to know you properly, and we want you to get a real feel for us too. If there's anything we can do to make the process work better for you, tell us.

We'd love to hear from you.

📍 Location & practical details

This is an on-site role based in Copenhagen. Only candidates currently located in Copenhagen, or those who clearly state in their application that they plan to relocate, will be considered.

Please note:

• 
We do not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

• 
We do not offer relocation services.

🔐 Data privacy (GDPR)

Applications for this role are processed exclusively through The Hub (thehub.io), our recruitment platform, in accordance with their privacy policy and applicable GDPR requirements. As part of our interview process, conversations may be recorded and transcribed via Microsoft Teams, and AI tools may be used to summarise interview notes to support our hiring team's evaluation. Your data will be handled confidentially, retained only during the interview process, and used only for this recruitment process.

For more information or questions please contact us at iva@flexecharge.com

Working at

FLEXECHARGE

FLEXECHARGE is a cleantech scale-up which offers a powerful load & energy management platform, as a SaaS, to help Charge Point Operators (ex: Clever, eOn, etc.) to optimise their charging operations & business. Our mission is accelerate green mobility through our Smart Charging solutions that make charging faster, greener and cheaper. Our vision is to integrate charging infrastructures better with the grid supply and the ever more volatile & growing production of renewable energy. We want to connect electric vehicles with the grid in a whole new way. By seeing electric vehicles not as a risk for our supply grid, but as a crucial asset for the transition towards 100% renewable energy. We do this through constant innovation of new smart charging features which will make us the preferred partner for EV infrastructure owners, developers, and operators.

Department: DMPK and Modelling Sciences

Location: [Måløv]

Your impact begins here

As a Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics (PKPD) Senior Principal Scientist, you will shape how translational modelling supports decisions across drug discovery and development. You will set direction for PKPD strategies, connect preclinical evidence with human safety and efficacy, and help interdisciplinary teams progress a diverse research portfolio. Your scientific leadership will strengthen project decisions from early research through clinical development and regulatory submission.

What you’ll bring

You bring deep expertise in translational science and mathematical modelling, together with the judgement to turn complex evidence into clear recommendations. You communicate effectively across disciplines, work independently and help colleagues solve scientific challenges.

• A PhD in pharmaceutical, medical, physical, mathematical or engineering sciences, or another relevant discipline, combined with substantial pharmaceutical industry experience.

• Ideally, at least ten years of relevant experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

• Strong knowledge and hands-on experience in PKPD, quantitative systems pharmacology and/or physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling.

• Experience developing mechanistic models, or combinations of mechanistic and empirical models, to represent biological or other natural processes.

• Practical experience with pharmacokinetic and modelling software such as Phoenix WinNonlin/NLME, NONMEM or an equivalent platform, and with analytical tools such as R, Python or MATLAB.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence decisions and collaborate across scientific disciplines.

Useful, but not essential: Experience with machine-learning workflows, managing external service providers, or supporting due diligence within physiologically based pharmacokinetic and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modelling.

What you’ll do

• Set the direction for translational PKPD screening and mechanistic modelling across different molecular formats, working with research, non-clinical and clinical stakeholders.

• Design preclinical PKPD/pharmacodynamic studies, interpret the results and communicate conclusions that support project decisions.

• Build mathematical models and run simulations of human PKPD using in-house in vitro and animal data, together with relevant literature.

• Guide project teams on preclinical study design, dose setting for toxicity studies, first-in-human dose selection and clinical trial design.

• Contribute scientific input to regulatory interactions and documents, including Investigational New Drug applications, Investigational Medicinal Product Dossiers and New Drug Applications.

• Advance scientific capabilities in mechanistic modelling and PKPD, solve complex problems and mentor fellow scientists.

Who you’ll work with

You will join one of two closely connected PKPD teams within DMPK and Modelling Sciences. Together, the teams advance the use of quantitative systems pharmacology, physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling and PKPD modelling across the research and development value chain.

Your closest collaborators will include in vivo pharmacologists, in vitro biologists, clinical modelling scientists, toxicologists, clinicians and regulatory affairs specialists. The area is part of Global Research within Research & Development and works with global discovery and development colleagues, project teams and external partners.

What you can expect here

You can expect a scientifically ambitious environment where knowledge-sharing and collaboration are part of the everyday work. You will have room to build your scientific and personal capabilities while contributing expertise that informs preclinical studies, first-in-human trials, clinical development and regulatory submissions. The role offers broad exposure across therapeutic areas and across the development pathway, from early research to submission.

jobs.description:
The Aarhus Laboratory Astrochemistry Group is seeking applications for a postdoctoral position in laboratory astrochemistry under supervision of Prof. Liv Hornekær at the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Aarhus University.

Job description
The successful applicants will participate in the experimental research activities under ERC Synergy Grant IRAstro and DNRF Center of Excellence for Interstellar Catalysis – InterCat. This combined project aims at elucidating how molecules on interstellar dust grain analogue surfaces organize, react and dissipate energy under low temperature and low pressure conditions mimicking dense interstellar dust and molecular clouds. The applicant will use low temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), temperature programmed desorption, and (single molecule) IR spectroscopy to follow in situ reactions leading to complex molecule formation on realistic dust grain analogue surfaces. Close collaboration with theoreticians, observers and the experimental astrochemistry groups at Aarhus University and at the nodes of collaborative partners is expected.

The job includes:

• Mapping of catalytic pathways and reaction rates on interstellar dust grain analogue surfaces using STM, TPD, and RAIRS. 
• development, maintenance and troubleshooting on various experimental UHV setups
• participating in maintenance of the group laboratories.
• data analysis and writing scientific publications.
• supervision of PhD, Master and bachelor students.
• project administration, such as writing reports etc.
 
Qualifications
Candidates should have a PhD degree in physics or similar field, with strong experience in experimental surface science, UHV techniques, catalysis/reactions on surfaces and atomic scale characterization. A background in laboratory astrochemistry is preferred.

The ideal candidate has good collaboration skills and is also able to work independently.

About IRAstro - Molecular Quantum Dynamics in Low-Temperature Astrochemistry 
The ERC Synergy project IRAstro brings together leading researchers in physics, chemistry, and astrochemistry to uncover how molecules behave and react under the extreme conditions of interstellar space.

Recent observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) reveal the complexity of low temperature molecular ices frozen out on interstellar dust grains in regions where new stars and planetary systems are formed. Interpreting these observations requires a deeper understanding of the fundamental physical and chemical processes that govern molecular behaviour at temperatures close to absolute zero.

IRAstro addresses this challenge by combining cutting-edge laboratory experiments, advanced instrumentation, and first-principles theory. The project focuses on the quantum dynamics of molecules in low-temperature condensed phases - a frontier area essential for understanding how chemical complexity arises in space.

https://phys.au.dk/irastro

About InterCat – Center for Interstellar Catalysis 
InterCat is a center of excellence supported by the Danish National Research Foundation. The center is situated at the Department of Physics and Astronomy and at the Interdisciplinary Nanoscience Center at Aarhus University in Denmark, at Leiden Observatory at Leiden University in the Netherlands and Niels Bohr Institute at University of Copenhagen in Denmark. See https://phys.au.dk/intercat/ for further details.

The scientific aim of the Center for Interstellar Catalysis is to determine whether the production of the molecular building blocks of life, e.g., sugars, amino acids, fats and DNA bases, predates the formation of stars and planets, and occurs at the extremely low temperatures and pressures found in interstellar space. InterCat thus aims to determine the molecular starting conditions for the origin of life across the universe.

InterCat brings together research teams within surface science, nanoscience, heterogeneous catalysis and experimental and observational astrochemistry.

jobs.description:
We are offering a three-year PhD fellowship in protein analysis commencing Feb 1, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  Research group
 This PhD project is a collaborative project between the lab of Professor Petrine Wellendorph (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, specializing in molecular pharmacology, principal supervisor), the Protein Analysis Group of Professor Kasper D. Rand (Department of Pharmacy, specializing in HDX-MS, principal co-supervisor), and Associate Professor Annette E. Langkilde (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, specialist in SAXS, co-supervisor). This interdisciplinary setup uniquely bridges brain mechanisms with protein dynamics and structure, enabling new biological insights and cross-fertilization between fields. The PhD fellowship is funded by a larger project grant from the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

  Project description
 Neuronal signalling underlies every function of the brain, from basic communication to learning and memory. This project focuses on a calcium-sensing protein that plays a central role in these processes. The project will apply in-solution biophysical and analytical methods to explore molecular details of ligand binding on protein dynamics to promote structure-function of the protein and, ultimately, advance drug discovery. As the primary methodology, mass spectrometry to measure the hydrogen/deuterium exchange (HDX-MS) of the protein in solution will be used. The HDX-MS method has emerged as a sensitive and powerful alternative technology to study the conformation of proteins using only small quantities of dilute samples. The project will utilize HDX-MS to analyze the protein in various conformational and activational states and elucidate its interaction with ligands and other proteins. Furthermore, the project will also use classical radioligand binding techniques and state-of-the-art biophysical methods e.g. DSF and SAXS to measure affinity and oligomerization. This combined experimental approach will allow for a detailed analysis of the biophysical, structural, and pharmacological properties of the protein.

  Principal supervisor
 Professor Petrine Wellendorph, Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, e-mail: pw@sund.ku.dk, tel. +45 3533 6397.

  As part of the assessment of whether you meet the educational requirements, you must also achieve a positive academic evaluation and be assessed as the best qualified for the position.

A good understanding of biochemistry and pharmacology is also a clear advantage. Preference will be given to applicants with experience in protein chemistry, mass spectrometry and data analysis. Experience with HDX-MS will give the applicant a particularly strong standing. As the project is highly collaborative, we are looking for applicants who are motivated to work across academic research groups and who bring strong interpersonal and communication skills to this kind of setting.

This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project to the Graduate School of Health and Medical Sciences.

Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31,800 DKK/Roughly 4,250 EUR (August 2026) plus pension.
